The year is 198X, and you're a jobbing composer. You start out with nothing but a toy keyboard shaped like a tiger, and a brand new sequence-o-matic 4-track that your uncle bought from a shady geezer in the pub.

Word quickly spreads about the new producer on the block, and soon the commissions are rolling in. Things start humble, recording tracks for weddings, workout videos and corporate presentations, but before long you're getting asked to score fantasy movies, museum openings, and all kinds of crazy stuff.

Of course, you'll have to upgrade your kit along the way. Turns out, the local second-hand magazine is a treasure trove of objects that make interesting sounds, from singing garden gnomes and shredders-that-shred-sound-as-well-as-paper, to high-end synthesisers and musical effects. By the end, you'll have figured out a sound that's all your own.


But OFFBEAT isn't just a game. All the musical instruments are fully simulated, and the music you're recording is real. The game is secretly a complete audio production tool. Every piece of music you create in the game gets exported and saved locally on your computer as a WAV file, which you use for whatever you want.

Music production can be costly and complex to get into, especially for beginners. We created OFFBEAT to lower barrier to entry and to offer a playful, low-pressure way to learn the basics of audio producion. The goal is just to be expressive and experimental, but by the end you'll have learned a little about synthesizers, sound design, composition and recording. Our hope is that when the game's finished, you'll have the confidence and expertise to carry on composing and recording music.


  • Game meets a real audio production tool.
  • Accept jobs, compose music, earn money. 
  • Browse the Riches & Rags Catalogue to buy new synthesizers, then get Electric Lacey to upgrade and mod 'em.
  • Make music in a low-pressure and beginner-friendly setting.
  • Meet a whole host of weird characters.
  • Export your tracks as a WAV files onto your computer.
  • Share your tracks with the world, or just friends – up to you. 
  • Play through chapters themed after different styles of electronic music.

--

Note 1: Your saved .wavs will appear here:  C:\Users\$USER\AppData\LocalLow\Whetstone Games\OFFBEAT\exported_audio

...but replace $USER with whatever your computer username is 

Note 2: Please wishlist OFFBEAT on Steam!

Rabertomg48 days ago(+2)

I’m really enjoying OFFBEAT. I think it’s an incredible way to gradually learn how music creation works while simply having fun playing.


One of the things I like the most is being able to experiment with rhythms, samples, and different combinations without needing advanced music production knowledge. Personally, it’s helping me a lot to understand how to build tracks, especially Drum & Bass, and some of the things you can create in the game sound genuinely amazing.


I also wanted to leave a small suggestion for the future: it would be really cool if the recordings or loops we create could be saved inside the game itself, almost like a personal library, so we could reuse them later with the mixer. I think it would add a lot of depth if we could gradually build our own collection of sounds and bring them back into new mixes or songs.


I’ve also been checking out the roadmap and I’m really looking forward to the upcoming updates. I’m especially excited for the Techno-related content planned for December, particularly the new machines and tools for creating that kind of music. If you can already make such cool stuff with the game now, I’m very curious to see how far that side of it will go.


Overall, I think OFFBEAT has a huge amount of potential. It’s not just entertaining — it actually makes you want to learn, experiment, and understand music production better.


Great work. I’m really looking forward to seeing how OFFBEAT continues to grow.
